label: ALPHA_NON_PRODUCTION

method.sources: public documentation, design guides, product pages only — no private product access
method.note: Scores are reasoned estimates from public materials, not lab usability tests. No evidence of live user study ⇒ usability PASS claims remain UNKNOWN until proof script + human protocol run.

competitors.name: Palantir Foundry Workshop
strongPatterns: F-shaped hierarchy; filters left, content right
Persistent module header / object views for consistent entity grammar
Overlays for secondary tasks; pages for primary workflows
weaknesses: Builder complexity; apps often diverge without design governance
Heavy ontology learning curve for new analysts
Can feel dense / enterprise-generic without Swiss restraint

competitors.name: Linkurious Enterprise
strongPatterns: Investigation-first graph canvas with alerts + case spaces
Collaboration / shared visualizations for team investigations
Pattern detection → alert triage → expand-in-graph loop
weaknesses: Enterprise packaging can hide simplicity for one-analyst flow

competitors.name: Neo4j Bloom
strongPatterns: Perspective = business view of graph (categories, styling, search phrases)
Scene actions for repeatable investigation moves
weaknesses: Graph-only product; not a full forensic OS flow
Weak citation / chain-of-custody UX out of the box

competitors.name: Maltego
strongPatterns: OSINT link analysis as primary mental model
weaknesses: Weak Swiss minimalism; limited institutional executive layer

competitors.name: Elastic Security
strongPatterns: Timeline as investigation workspace; drag fields into query
Timeline templates on detection rules (instant context)
Alert → Timeline → Case / notes without leaving product
Investigation guides with one-click prefilled queries
weaknesses: Graph/link analysis secondary vs SIEM table culture
Query languages (KQL/EQL) raise cognitive load for legal/client roles
Visual language is Kibana-generic, not Apple/Swiss forensic brand

competitors.name: Splunk Enterprise Security (public UX patterns)
strongPatterns: Notable events / risk-based alerting as triage spine
weaknesses: Classic dashboard density; high training cost

strongestPatternsAcrossMarket.pattern: F-shaped layout: filters/nav left, primary canvas center/right
strongestPatternsAcrossMarket.adoptForSciOs: Keep Graph/Timeline canvas dominant; inspector panel secondary (Design System 12-col)

strongestPatternsAcrossMarket.pattern: Consistent entity/object view wherever an ID appears
strongestPatternsAcrossMarket.adoptForSciOs: One entity inspector grammar across Graph, Timeline, Evidence
Canonical UX Flow: Graph→Timeline→Evidence with deep links + carry-over

strongestPatternsAcrossMarket.pattern: Timeline is a workspace, not a chart widget
strongestPatternsAcrossMarket.adoptForSciOs: Timeline View owns temporal investigation; templates for common case types
Swiss–Apple: Snow White, Fog Grey, Deep Navy; no dashboard chrome soup
Dossier + Client Portal as trust layers, not extra graph tools

weaknessesToAvoid: Query-first UX for non-analyst roles (client, executive)
Module-by-module visual reinvention (Palantir governance failure mode)
Fake READY / density that signals power but blocks time-to-insight
Graph-only products without evidence citation and dossier export
SIEM table culture without spatial Graph entry for forensic narrative

differentiators: Swiss-grade auditability + citation on AI outputs
Role-split surfaces (analyst vs client vs executive) with same case context
Tesla-level simplicity: one primary action per view
120 FPS motion / 300ms macro transitions with reduced-motion support
No parallel Atom/AI stub trees — one cockpit language
workflowAccelerationRules: Deep link every view with case + selection query params
Single primary CTA per view; secondary in inspector
Evidence selection always shows provenance / hash when available
